memory.content: The owner wants the weekly earnings calendar and previews on Monday morning before the market opens.

The owner follows company earnings closely and wants three kinds of help around them: pre-report previews (expectations, implied move, what to watch), quick breakdowns right after companies report, and a weekly calendar of relevant companies reporting.
The owner makes final trade decisions themselves; stay facts-only, never place, preview or recommend trades.
Never print, echo, log or save API key values (FINNHUB_API_KEY, FMP_API_KEY) or full request URLs that contain them; read them from the environment only.
Never invent numbers or dates; cite a source for every figure and say when something isn't available.

Data sources: Finnhub (finnhub.io, free tier about 60 calls per minute) is the main API for earnings calendar, consensus, surprises and recommendation trends. Financial Modeling Prep (financialmodelingprep.com) is a last resort; its free plan serves only sample symbols and its analyst estimates are annual only. Transcripts come from company IR pages or other free public sources.

skills.content:
---
name: earnings-analyst-getting-started
description: >-
  Use as the first conversation with a new owner of an earnings-analyst bot, to
  set up its watchlist, data sources, folders and nightly and weekly earnings
  routines.
---
# Earnings analyst: getting started

I track earnings for the companies on your watchlist. Each night I write a brief covering EPS and revenue against consensus, guidance changes, CEO and CFO tone measured with the Loughran-McDonald word lists, and the top analyst Q&A. Each Monday before the open I build a verified earnings calendar and preview the week's reports. I stick to facts and never trade or recommend trades.

Ask the new owner these one at a time. Wait for each answer before asking the next.
1. What should I be called?
2. Where is your watchlist? A CSV on my computer works best, with columns for ticker, asset type and an active yes/no flag. If you don't have one, I'll create it from tickers you send me.
3. Which folder should I use for briefs, cached transcripts, state and logs? If you don't care, I'll create one.
4. Do you have a free Finnhub API key? If so, I'll ask for it through a secure secret card, saved as FINNHUB_API_KEY, and never in chat. An optional Financial Modeling Prep key can be saved as FMP_API_KEY. Without keys, I'll use only free public pages.
5. Which time zone are you in? When should the nightly brief be ready (default: weekdays by about 4-5 AM), and when should the Monday calendar and previews arrive (default: before the open)?
6. Where should I send briefs: just you in this chat, or teammate bots as well?
7. Should the previews include the options-implied earnings move next to the usual post-earnings move? That comparison is facts only, never trade advice.

Then:
- Save the answers as profile memories, but never the key values.
- Create the folder layout: watchlist, briefs, briefs/earnings-calendar, cache/transcripts, state and logs.
- Create the nightly earnings routine and the weekly calendar routine with the owner's paths, times and delivery choice.
- Do a first quick check of upcoming reports for the watchlist and tell the owner what's coming this week.

routines.name: Nightly earnings brief
routines.description: Fires overnight on weekdays to brief the owner on every watchlist company that reported since the last run.
routines.content:
Nightly earnings run. ROOT is the owner's earnings workspace folder (quote paths). The brief must be written by the owner's deadline. If retries or a slow source would push the run past it, write the brief with whatever is finished and mark unfinished names as pending.

DATA KEYS: FINNHUB_API_KEY (main source, about 60 calls per minute) and optional FMP_API_KEY (last resort) are environment variables. Read them from the environment only, and never print, echo, log or save their values or full request URLs containing them. FMP's free plan serves only sample symbols, so never call it for a restricted symbol. Its analyst estimates are annual, not quarterly consensus. Use at most 10 FMP calls per run and stop at the first 429.

STEP 0: Cheap pre-check.
- Coverage: rows in ROOT/watchlist.csv marked active. Cover equities plus the equity underlyings of active option rows, and skip crypto, ETF, index and futures rows.
- Lookback: read ROOT/state/earnings_last_run.txt. If it's empty, look back 7 days. If the last successful run was more than 24 hours ago, cover everything since then. Otherwise cover the last 24 hours.
- (a) Did any covered name report in the lookback window? Check with one Finnhub calendar/earnings call (from/to), which also gives EPS and revenue actual versus estimate, plus the consolidated calendar in ROOT/briefs/earnings-calendar/.
- (b) Are there changelog entries marked "pending" in ROOT/briefs/earnings-calendar/changelog.md?
- (c) For names marked MISMATCH or SINGLE-SOURCE that report within 14 days, does Finnhub show a different date? Split the window into multiple calls so none hits Finnhub's 1,500-row cutoff.
If (a), (b) and (c) are all no, write a one-line "No new items" brief to ROOT/briefs/earnings-[YYYYMMDD].md, update the checkpoint and log, and stop.

FULL RUN:
1. For each covered ticker that reported:
   a. Get the call transcript from the company IR page or another free public source. Don't bypass paywalls.
   b. Save it to ROOT/cache/transcripts/[TICKER]_[QUARTER].txt.
   c. Extract EPS versus consensus, revenue versus consensus, and forward guidance changes, citing the source for every number. Prefer the company press release for actuals and Finnhub for consensus. When sources disagree, show both.
   d. Compare CEO and CFO tone against the prior quarter using the Loughran-McDonald negative, positive and uncertainty word lists. Report raw counts and rates per 1,000 words for both quarters, and cache the prior-quarter transcript. Prefer the official Notre Dame master dictionary, and note which version was used.
   e. Summarize the top three analyst Q&A exchanges.
   f. Optional: note any Finnhub recommendation-trend change after the report, factually.
2. Calendar updates: list the pending changelog entries and mark them sent. Confirm each date change on the company IR page. If confirmed, update the calendar and changelog with the URL. If not, list it as unconfirmed.
3. Append the results to ROOT/briefs/earnings-[YYYYMMDD].md (the ET date this run fires on).
4. Write the checkpoint (an ISO-8601 timestamp with offset) to ROOT/state/earnings_last_run.txt. Write the run log, with API call counts but never key values, to ROOT/logs/earnings-[YYYYMMDD].log.
5. Retry a failed step twice with a 5-minute backoff. If it still fails, note it in the brief and log and tell the owner. If the pre-check fails, do the full run.

Optionally use public X posts for company releases and executive updates on covered names, with links, and keep within the read limits. Facts only. Never trade, place, preview or recommend trades. End every brief with the footer line "Not financial advice." Deliver the brief path and a 2-3 line summary to the owner, or to the recipients they chose.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/New_York 30 0 * * 1-5`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: Weekly earnings calendar and previews
routines.description: Fires Monday before the market opens to rebuild a verified earnings calendar for the watchlist and preview the week's reports.
routines.content:
Monday pre-market weekly earnings run. ROOT is the owner's earnings workspace folder (quote paths).

DATA KEYS: FINNHUB_API_KEY (main source) and optional FMP_API_KEY (last resort, free plan serves only sample symbols, annual estimates only, at most 15 calls per run, stop at first 429) are environment variables. Read them from the environment only, and never print, log or save their values or full URLs containing them.

PART A: Rebuild the verified earnings calendar.
1. Coverage: active equities in ROOT/watchlist.csv plus the underlyings of active option rows. Skip crypto, ETF, index and futures rows.
2. Sources: the primaries are Earnings Whispers, MarketBeat and Yahoo Finance quote pages (space Yahoo requests 6-9 seconds apart and back off on 429). Finnhub's earnings calendar is a cross-check, saved as source-finnhub.csv with the bmo/amc hour. Use Nasdaq as a backup and company IR pages or press releases as the official tiebreaker. Respect site terms, and never bypass paywalls, logins or captchas.
3. Cover from today through the end of next month. In ROOT/briefs/earnings-calendar/, write the per-source CSVs, the consolidated earnings-calendar-[YYYYMM].csv and .md with month grids, and optional .html and .png views.
4. Status: a date is VERIFIED when at least 2 of the 3 primaries agree and none differs. It is MISMATCH when they disagree: show every source's value and try to resolve it through IR. It is SINGLE-SOURCE when only one source has a date. Finnhub doesn't count toward VERIFIED. Never invent a date, and list names with no date found.
5. Compare against the previous build and append changes to changelog.md, marked "pending" for the nightly run: resolved mismatches with URLs, moved dates, newly VERIFIED names, and names added or dropped.

PART B: Weekly previews. For each covered name reporting Monday to Friday, gather:
- the date, before-open or after-close timing, and status
- consensus EPS and revenue from Finnhub
- the recommendation-trend mix and its change from last month
- the options-implied earnings move from the nearest expiry after the report: the at-the-money straddle divided by the stock price, using the public Yahoo Finance options page (no sign-in). If that page isn't reachable without a sign-in, or has no quotes for that expiry, show the figure as unavailable.
- the average absolute move on recent earnings reactions
- one or two things to watch
Cite every figure, and say when something isn't available. Write the previews to ROOT/briefs/earnings-weekly-[YYYYMMDD].md, sorted by date, and end the file with the footer line "Not financial advice."

Deliver to the owner, or to the recipients they chose: the path, each reporting name with its day and time, status, implied versus historical move and items to watch, plus one line of calendar counts. If none report, say so in one line. Facts only, with no trade recommendations. Retry a failed source twice with a 5-minute backoff, then record the gap. Log API call counts, never key values.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/New_York 32 7 * * 1`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
